definition_zh: 混合；混杂；交往；与……打成一片；交融
definition_en: to mix or blend together, or to move among people and talk with them
core_image: 两股不同颜色的颜料在杯子里慢慢搅到一起，分不清你我
scene: 宴会上，各个行业的人端着杯在厅里走动交谈。At the reception, guests from many trades mingle and exchange business cards.
sceneCN: 这里 mingle 是「交往、打成一片」（第 3 个义项：在人群中走动交谈）；句意：招待会上，各行各业的人在人群中交谈并交换名片。

pos.zh: 混合；混杂；交往；打成一片

derivatives.zh: 混合；交往，由 mingle 加 -ing 构成的名词形
mingle 的第三人称单数，词族内的规则变形
混合；掺和，由前缀 com- 与 mingle 组合而成

senses.title: To mix so that things blend
senses.definition: to combine two or more things so that they become one mixed whole
senses.definitionCN: 把两种或更多事物合在一起，形成一个难以分开的整体
senses.example: The two rivers mingle near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 两条河在近海处汇流交融。
senses.why: The core image is physical stirring: separate things lose their clear edges once they share one container.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是搅拌：一旦同处一个容器，原本分开的东西就失去了清晰的边界。

senses.title: To be mixed with something
senses.definition: to appear together with something else, especially feelings or sounds that are hard to separate
senses.definitionCN: 与别的事物同时出现，尤指难以分开的情绪或声音
senses.example: Joy mingled with sadness as they left the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 离开老屋时，喜悦中夹杂着悲伤。
senses.why: From mixing substances the verb moved on to mixing immaterial things such as feelings and voices.
senses.whyCN: 动词从混合实体延伸到混合感受、声音等非物质事物。

senses.title: To move among people and talk
senses.definition: to move around among a group of people and talk with them socially
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中间走动，并与之社交交谈
senses.example: The host mingled with guests near the door.
senses.exampleCN: 主人站在门口与客人们交谈。
senses.why: People who move freely in a group mix the way liquids do, so the social sense grew straight out of the mixing image.
senses.whyCN: 人在群体中自由走动就像液体互溶，社交义正是从混合意象直接长出来的。

senses.title: To blend into a crowd
senses.definition: to become part of a group or crowd without standing out
senses.definitionCN: 成为群体的一部分而不引人注目
senses.example: He lowered his cap and mingled into the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 他压低帽子，混进了人群。
senses.why: The mixing sense turns into deliberate camouflage: a person who blends in is no longer a visible drop.
senses.whyCN: 混合义转为有意的隐藏：融入者不再是看得见的那一滴。

senses.title: In bars: to combine spirits
senses.definition: to stir or pour drinks together so that their flavours blend
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的酒或饮品搅在一起，使味道融合
senses.example: The bartender mingled gin with a little tonic.
senses.exampleCN: 调酒师把金酒和少许汤力水调在一起。
senses.why: Alcoholic mixing is the most literal everyday use of the stir-together image.
senses.whyCN: 调酒是「搅在一起」这个意象最字面的日常用法。

senses.title: Genetics: to interbreed
senses.definition: to breed or marry across different groups so that their traits combine
senses.definitionCN: 在不同群体间繁殖或通婚，使双方特征结合
senses.example: The wild flocks had mingled with farm birds for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 野生鸟群与农场禽鸟杂交已有数十年。
senses.why: Combining family lines is mixing at the level of inherited material.
senses.whyCN: 家族血脉的结合，是遗传层面的混合。

intro.en: Mingle probably comes from Old English mengan, meaning to mix, with the frequentative ending -l-, and is first recorded in the 1400s.
intro.cn: mingle 一般认为源自古英语 mengan（混合），带表反复的后缀 -l-，首见于十五世纪。

items.en: Mengan means to mix or stir things together.
items.cn: mengan 意为混合、搅在一起。

items.en: The form minglen appears with the ending l, suggesting repeated mixing.
items.cn: meng(e)n 加了词尾 l 出现为 minglen，暗示反复混合。

items.en: Mingle extends from substances to people who mix in company.
items.cn: 至十六世纪，mingle 从物质扩展到在人群中交往的人。

items.en: Abstract use grows: feelings, sounds, and rumours mingle.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，抽象用法增多：情绪、声音、传闻都能 mingling。

items.en: Modern English adds commingle and the social sense of joining a crowd.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了 commingle，以及「融入人群」的社交义。

note.en: Mingle is the stir-together verb, close to its prefix-built relative and to other mixing words at a party.
note.cn: mingle 是「搅在一起」的动词，与带前缀的同族词以及各种「混合」词相邻。

entries.definition: to mix together completely
the act of mixing or socialising
an old name for a confused jumble
entries.definitionCN: 旧时形容杂乱的一堆东西

entries.definition: to mix smoothly into one substance
to spend time with other people in a group
the general verb for combining things

normalIntro.en: Mingle is a stirring word: things or people share one space and their edges blur.
normalIntro.cn: mingle 是一个「搅拌」词：事物或人共处一处，边界随之模糊。

normal.en: Mingle with someone is to chat among them.
normal.cn: mingle with someone 就是与对方攀谈。

normal.en: Commingle adds com- to the same base.
normal.cn: commingle 只是在同一词基前加了 com-。

normal.en: Mingled feelings are mixed feelings.
normal.cn: mingled feelings 就是混杂的心情。

normal.en: The old mengan meant to mix, and it still shows.
normal.cn: 古英语 mengan 意为混合，这层意思仍留在词里。

normal.en: Compare mix: mix works for recipes, mingle is softer and more social.
normal.cn: 对比 mix：mix 更像配方用语，mingle 更柔和、更社交。

abstract.en: Picture two paint drops swirling into one colour.
abstract.cn: 想象两滴颜料旋转着融成一种颜色。

abstract.en: See a newcomer stepping into a circle of talkers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新人走进一圈正在交谈的人中。

abstract.en: Hear laughter and music blurring into one sound.
abstract.cn: 想象笑声与音乐混成一片声音。

examples.en: Students mingle easily after the first workshop.
examples.cn: 第一次工作坊之后，学生们很容易打成一片。

examples.en: The smell of coffee mingled with fresh bread.
examples.cn: 咖啡的香气与新鲜面包的味道交融。

examples.en: She stood at the edge, too shy to mingle.
examples.cn: 她站在边上，羞于与人交往。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「明哥」——明哥在酒会上到处跟人碰杯聊天，把全场混成一团；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 mengan（混合）→ 带反复后缀 -l- 的 mingl(e)n → 现代英语 mingle，核心义「搅在一起、彼此交融」。

sensesIntro.en: Mingle begins as stirring substances into one, then spreads to feelings, to people mixing at events, and to other kinds of combining.
sensesIntro.cn: mingle 起初指把物质搅成一体，随后扩展到情绪，再到人们在活动中呼朋接伴，以及各种形式的结合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two colours stirred into one cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种颜色在杯中搅成一种。

branches.en: Physical stirring and drink-making are the most literal uses.
branches.cn: 物理搅拌与调酒是这个词最字面的用法。

branches.en: Feelings and sounds mingle like liquids that cannot be untangled.
branches.cn: 情绪与声音像液体一样交融，再也分不开。

branches.en: People mixing at a party borrow the same image for social life.
branches.cn: 宴会上的人把同一意象借给社交生活。

branches.en: Blending in turns mixing into deliberate camouflage.
branches.cn: 融入人群把混合变成有意的隐藏。

branches.en: Breeding across groups is mixing blood and family lines.
branches.cn: 群体间的杂交通婚是血脉与家族的混合。

intro.en: Mingle is a native verb built from mengan plus the frequentative l, while commingle adds the Latin prefix com-.
intro.cn: mingle 是由 mengan 加反复后缀 -l- 构成的本族动词，commingle 则加了拉丁语前缀 com-。

latinIntro.en: Mingle is not Latin in origin, although the Latin prefix com- later joined it inside commingle.
latinIntro.cn: mingle 并非源自拉丁语，只是后来在 commingle 中接上了拉丁前缀 com-。

items.example: Mengan is the older English verb for mixing.
items.exampleCN: mengan 是较早的英语「混合」动词。

items.example: The -l- ending adds the idea of repeated stirring.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -l- 增添了反复搅拌的意味。

items.example: Mingle covers both blending and meeting people.
items.exampleCN: mingle 同时涵盖混合与社交。

items.example: Commingle is the formal partner of mingle.
items.exampleCN: commingle 是 mingle 的正式说法。

items.example: The prefix com- means together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 com- 意为「一起」。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为的动名词
items.example: The suffix -ing forms mingling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 mingling。

items.example: Mingling happened near the buffet.
items.exampleCN: 交际活动发生在自助餐台附近。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms mingled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 mingled。

items.example: Mingled describes mixed feelings.
items.exampleCN: mingled 用来形容交织的心情。

items.example: Mingle with turns the verb social.
items.exampleCN: mingle with 让动词带上社交色彩。

definition_zh: 使降到最低；把……减到最少；使最小；缩小；把……看轻；把窗口最小化
definition_en: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount, size, or importance
core_image: 一只手把音量旋钮一圈圈向左拧，数字越变越小，直到底
scene: 暴雨夜，书店老板把所有书搬离地面，又用塑料布封住窗户，想把损失压到最低。The bookseller moved every box onto high shelves and taped plastic over the windows to minimise the damage from the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 minimise 是「使降到最低；把损失减到最少」（第 1 个义项：把数量或程度降到尽可能小）；句意：书店老板把所有箱子搬到高架上，又用胶带把塑料布封在窗户上，想把这场暴风雨造成的损失降到最低。

pos.zh: 使降到最低；把……减到最少；使最小

derivatives.zh: minimise + -ation，义为「最小化；减到最低的过程」
由拉丁词干 minim- 直接构成，义为「最小值；最少的」
minim- + -al，义为「极少的；最小的」，如 minimal damage
同一动词的美式拼写，词尾 -ize 与英式 -ise 对应
minimise + -er，义为「把事物减到最小的人或装置」
minimal + -ist，义为「极简主义者；极简风格的」，与 minimise 共同表示「少到不能再少」

senses.title: To reduce to the smallest amount
senses.titleCN: 使降到最低；把……减到最少
senses.definition: to reduce the amount, size, or degree of something as much as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的数量、规模或程度尽可能降低
senses.example: We need to minimise the risk of fire in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要把厨房起火的风险降到最低。
senses.why: Latin minimus means smallest, and the suffix -ise means to make, so the word literally means to make smallest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minimus 意为「最小的」，后缀 -ise 表示「使……」，所以这个词字面就是「使成为最小」，核心画面是旋钮被一路拧小。

senses.title: To make light of something
senses.definition: to treat a problem, fault, or loss as less serious or less important than it is
senses.definitionCN: 把问题、过错或损失看得比实际情况轻
senses.example: The manager tried to minimise the seriousness of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 经理试图淡化这起事故的严重性。
senses.why: If the thing being reduced is not a number but a fault or a loss, the same downward gesture becomes shrinking its importance.
senses.whyCN: 要缩小的东西从数字变成了过错或损失，同一个「往下压」的动作就变成了压低它的分量，所以这个义项侧重「大事化小」。

senses.title: To shrink a window on screen
senses.definition: to make a computer window smaller than usual and hide it at the bottom of the screen
senses.definitionCN: 把电脑窗口缩到最小并收到屏幕底部的任务栏里
senses.example: Minimise the window so you can read the message behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 把窗口最小化，这样你就能看到它后面的消息了。
senses.why: On a screen the smallest possible size is a button on the bottom bar, so software turns the old image of the smallest reachable setting into a click.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上，能缩到的最小形态就是收成底栏上的一个按钮，所以软件把这个词原本「降到最小」的画面变成了看得见的一次点击。

intro.en: Minimise is a modern verb formed from Latin minimus, smallest, with the English suffix -ise meaning to make.
intro.cn: minimise 是现代英语用拉丁语 minimus（最小的）加英语后缀 -ise（使……）构成的动词。

items.en: Minimus is the superlative of parvus, small, and means the smallest.
items.cn: minimus 是 parvus（小的）的最高级，意为「最小的」。

items.en: Minimum is used as a noun for the smallest amount and is borrowed into English.
items.cn: minimum 在拉丁语中作名词，指「最小的量」，后被英语借用。

items.en: Minimum appears in English first as a mathematical and scientific term.
items.cn: minimum 最早在十七世纪以数学与科技术语的身份进入英语。

items.en: The verbs minimise and minimize are formed, first in mathematics and economics.
items.cn: 动词形式 minimise 与 minimize 出现，最初用于数学与经济学。

items.en: Minimise spreads to management, design, and computing, including the window button.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到管理、设计以及计算机领域，包括窗口上的那个按钮。

note.en: Minimise belongs to the Latin par- and minim- family, with minimum, minimal, and minimise, and it stands near words for reducing and cutting things down.
note.cn: minimise 属于表示「小」的词族，与 minimum、minimal 同源；在意义上与表示减少、削减的词相邻，但强调「压到底」这一终点。

entries.definition: the smallest amount that is possible
as small as possible
the same verb spelled with -ize
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写，词尾写作 -ize

entries.definition: to make smaller in size, amount, or number
to reduce an amount, especially money or time
to control or limit something harmful

normalIntro.en: Minimise pairs the Latin root minim-, meaning smallest, with the suffix -ise, which means to make.
normalIntro.cn: minimise 由拉丁词根 minim-（最小的）加后缀 -ise（使……）组成，天生就是「使它变成最小」的意思。

normal.en: Latin minimus means smallest, so minim- carries the idea of the lower limit.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 minimus 意为「最小的」，所以词根 minim- 带着「下限」的意味。

normal.en: The suffix -ise turns adjectives and nouns into verbs meaning to make or cause.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ise 把形容词或名词变成「使……；造成……」的动词，如 minimise、modernise。

normal.en: Compare minimum and minimise: minimum is the bottom value, minimise is the act of getting there.
normal.cn: 对比 minimum 与 minimise：minimum 是底部的那个值，minimise 是往下压到底的动作。

normal.en: Business writing has ready pairs such as minimise costs and minimise risks.
normal.cn: 商务写作里有现成的搭配：把成本减到最少、把风险降到最低。

normal.en: British writing uses -ise, American writing uses -ize, so minimisation and minimization are the same noun.
normal.cn: 英式写 -ise，美式写 -ize，所以 minimisation 与 minimization 是同一个名词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand turning a volume knob slowly to the left until the number reads zero.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把音量旋钮慢慢向左拧，数字一直减到零。

abstract.en: Imagine waving a fault away with both hands, as if it were only a little smoke.
abstract.cn: 想象用双手把一处过错轻轻扇开，好像它只是一缕小烟，这就是把过错看轻。

abstract.en: Think of a window sliding down to a thin line at the bottom of the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个窗口滑落，最后缩成屏幕底部的一条细线。

examples.en: Careful planning can minimise the risk of losing data.
examples.cn: 周密的计划可以把数据丢失的风险降到最低。

examples.en: The airline minimised the delay by changing planes.
examples.cn: 航空公司通过换飞机把延误减到了最少。

examples.en: Minimise the window if you want to see the desktop.
examples.cn: 如果你想看到桌面，就把窗口最小化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你卖子」——小店铺里小声地卖东西，越卖越少，最后缩到「迷你」大小；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 parvus（小的）→ 最高级 minimus（最小的）→ 拉丁 minimum（最小的量）→ 英语 minimise（使降到最低），核心义「压到底线」。

sensesIntro.en: Minimise begins with amounts that can be lowered, widens to faults whose weight can be played down, then moves to a computing use that shrinks a window to a button.
sensesIntro.cn: minimise 先从可以调低的数量起步，扩展到可以压低分量的过错，最后用于让窗口缩成屏幕底栏上的按钮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned all the way down to the lowest mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋钮被一路拧到刻度的最低处。

branches.en: Amounts pushed to their floor give the base sense.
branches.cn: 把数量压到下限，是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: A fault shrunk in importance is the attitude sense.
branches.cn: 把过错的分量压小，是这个词的态度义项。

branches.en: A window shrunk to a bar button is the computing sense.
branches.cn: 窗口缩成底栏按钮，是这个词的计算机义项。

branches.en: Costs and blame are both lowered to a point where little more can be cut.
branches.cn: 成本与责难都被压到再无可减的地步，二者同源。

branches.en: Waste and windows are both made small on purpose.
branches.cn: 浪费与窗口都是被人为缩小的，只是一个涉及资源，一个涉及界面。

intro.en: Minimise is built on the Latin superlative stem minim-, to which English adds the verb suffix -ise, as it does in modernise and optimise.
intro.cn: minimise 由拉丁最高级词干 minim- 加英语动词后缀 -ise 构成，和 modernise、optimise 的构词方式一样。

latinIntro.en: Latin parvus means small, minimus means smallest, and the noun minimum means the smallest thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 parvus 意为「小的」，minimus 意为「最小的」，名词 minimum 意为「最小的东西」。

items.example: The stem minim- appears in minimum, minimal, and minimise.
items.exampleCN: 词干 minim- 出现在 minimum、minimal 与 minimise 里。

items.example: Parvus is the positive form behind the superlative minimus.
items.exampleCN: parvus 是最高级 minimus 的原级。

items.example: Minimus is the superlative of parvus.
items.exampleCN: minimus 是 parvus 的最高级。

items.example: Minimum is the noun from which the verb was built.
items.exampleCN: minimum 是这个动词所依托的名词。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ise turns minimum into an action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把 minimum 变成动作。

items.example: Minimize is the American spelling of the same verb.
items.exampleCN: minimize 是同一动词的美式拼写。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms minimisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 minimisation，表示最小化的过程。

items.example: The suffix -al forms minimal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 minimal。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms minimizer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 minimizer。

items.meaning: a person who follows a practice
items.meaningCN: 表示奉行某种做法的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ist forms minimalist from minimal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 由 minimal 构成 minimalist。

definition_zh: 海市蜃楼；蜃景；幻景；（沙漠或公路上因热空气形成的）水影；幻想；假象
definition_en: an image of water or of distant objects that appears in hot air, or something pleasant that is not real
core_image: 滚烫的柏油路上浮出一片水光，走近却只剩热浪
scene: 正午的沙漠公路上，前方路面像积了一汪水，车子开近了却什么也没有。Heat rising from the sand made a mirage that looked like a lake just ahead.
sceneCN: 这里 mirage 是「海市蜃楼；蜃景」（第 1 个义项：热空气中出现的水影或远处景物的虚像）；句意：从沙子里升起的灼热空气形成了海市蜃楼，看上去前方就有一片湖。

pos.zh: 海市蜃楼；蜃景；热空气造成的水影

collocations.phrase: turn out to be a mirage

derivatives.zh: admire + -ation，义为「钦佩；赞赏」，与 mirage 同出拉丁语 mirari
mirage + -like，义为「像海市蜃楼一样的」，多用于文学描写
同出拉丁语 mirari（惊奇地看）的词，义为「镜子；反映」，与 mirage 共享「看」的词根
ad-（向）+ mirari（惊奇地看），义为「钦佩；欣赏」
由拉丁语 mirari 的动词形式 miror 演变而来，义为「奇迹」，与 mirage 同源

senses.title: An image made by hot air
senses.definition: an image of water or of distant objects that appears above hot ground because of the bending of light
senses.definitionCN: 热地面上的空气使光线偏折，因而出现的水影或远处景物的虚像
senses.example: The travellers saw a lake in the desert, but it was only a mirage.
senses.exampleCN: 旅人在沙漠里看到一片湖，但那只是海市蜃楼。
senses.why: French se mirer means to look at oneself in a mirror, and the noun was first given to the shimmering sheet that hot air lays over a road or a desert.
senses.whyCN: 法语 se mirer 意为「照镜自看」，这个词最早用来指热空气在公路或沙漠上铺开的那层闪光的水面，画面本身就是一面空气做的镜子。

senses.title: A pleasant thing that is not real
senses.definition: something that you hope for or seem to see but that does not exist or cannot be reached
senses.definitionCN: 人们希望得到或以为看见、实际上并不存在也无法实现的事物
senses.example: The promise of easy money was a mirage.
senses.exampleCN: 轻松赚钱的许诺只是一个泡影。
senses.why: Because the optical image always vanishes as you get near it, the word easily names any hope or plan that keeps retreating.
senses.whyCN: 因为那个光学影像越走近越会消失，很自然地就被人拿来指那些越是伸手越落空的希望和计划，所以这个义项侧重「看得见摸不着」。

intro.en: Mirage comes from French mirage, a noun of action from the old verb se mirer, to look at oneself in a mirror, and from Latin mirari, to wonder at.
intro.cn: mirage 来自法语名词 mirage，由古法语动词 se mirer（照镜自看）构成，源头是拉丁语 mirari（惊奇地看）。

items.en: Miror and mirari mean to wonder at or look at with wonder, and mirus means wonderful.
items.cn: miror 与 mirari 意为「惊奇地看」，mirus 意为「奇妙的」。

items.en: The reflexive verb se mirer means to look at oneself in a glass or mirror.
items.cn: 古法语反身动词 se mirer 意为「照镜子看自己」。

items.en: The noun mirage is formed and used for the shimmering image that hot air shows over water or sand.
items.cn: 名词 mirage 形成，用来指热气在水面或沙地上呈现的闪烁影像。

items.en: English borrows mirage first as a term of travel and geography for desert scenes.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪先把 mirage 作为旅行与地理术语借用过来，多指沙漠景象。

items.en: The word widens to any false hope, such as a mirage of peace or a mirage of growth.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展为任何虚假的希望，如和平的假象、增长的幻影。

note.en: Mirage belongs to the Latin mirari family, with mirror, admire, and miracle, and it stands near words for things seen or hoped for but not real.
note.cn: mirage 属于拉丁「惊奇地看」词族，与 mirror、admire、miracle 同源；在意义上与表示「看得见却不真实」的词相邻，但强调热空气把远处的景物折射成假象。

entries.definition: a piece of glass that shows you a reflection
entries.definitionCN: 镜子；反映，与 mirage 同出 mirari

entries.definition: to look at something with respect and pleasure
an event that seems impossible and is caused by a god
something that looks real but is not, especially a wrong idea about the world
something a person sees or hears that is not really there, because of illness or drugs
a ghost or an image of something that is not there

normalIntro.en: Mirage pairs the Latin root mir-, meaning to look at with wonder, with the French noun ending -age, so it names the trick that your eyes play when they wonder at a shining false lake.
normalIntro.cn: mirage 由拉丁词根 mir-（惊奇地看）加法语名词词尾 -age 组成，所以它指的就是眼睛在惊奇中看到的那片假湖。

normal.en: The root mir- appears in mirror and admire, both of which involve looking, and mirage is a false mirror made of air.
normal.cn: 词根 mir- 出现在 mirror 与 admire 里，都与「看」有关，而 mirage 就是一面空气做的假镜子。

normal.en: French se mirer means to look at oneself in a mirror, and the noun was first a name for vanishing water on a road.
normal.cn: 法语 se mirer 意为照镜子看自己，这个名词最初就是指公路上那片会消失的「水」。

normal.en: The suffix -age builds abstract nouns in French, as in voyage and mirage.
normal.cn: 词尾 -age 在法语里构成抽象名词，如 voyage 与 mirage。

normal.en: Useful pair: a mirage of water is a physical image, while a mirage of wealth is a false hope.
normal.cn: 好用的搭配对比：a mirage of water 是物理上的水影，a mirage of wealth 是虚假的希望。

normal.en: Compare with mirror: both share the root, but mir- in mirage points to a reflection that does not exist.
normal.cn: 与 mirror 对比：两者同根，但 mirage 里的 mir- 指向一个并不存在的倒影。

abstract.en: Picture a bright sheet of water lying on the road ahead, gone the moment the car reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象前方路面上铺着一片亮闪闪的水，车子一开到却什么也没有。

abstract.en: Think of a palm island and its green shade, floating above the sand and dissolving as you walk.
abstract.cn: 想象一座长着棕榈的小岛，浮在沙子上方，走过去就散了。

abstract.en: Imagine a glass of water offered to a thirsty traveller that slips out of his hand and becomes empty air.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把一杯水递给口渴的旅人，杯子滑出手心，变成了一阵空气。

examples.en: On the long drive they saw a mirage that looked like a river crossing the road.
examples.cn: 长途驾驶中他们看到一处海市蜃楼，像一条河横穿过公路。

examples.en: The steady rise in prices proved to be a mirage once the market fell.
examples.cn: 市场一跌，持续上涨的价格就被证明不过是假象。

examples.en: Rainfall that never came left the farmers chasing a mirage all summer.
examples.cn: 始终没有落下的雨水让农民整个夏天都在追逐一个幻影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密 拉 日」——太阳把炎热密密麻麻地拉成一片，就拉出远处的假水景；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mirari（惊奇地看）→ 古法语 se mirer（照镜自看）→ 法语名词 mirage（热气造成的假水影）→ 英语 mirage，核心义「看得见却摸不着」。

sensesIntro.en: Mirage starts as the optical image that hot air lays over sand or road, then widens to any false hope that keeps retreating as people approach it.
sensesIntro.cn: mirage 先是热空气在沙地或路面上铺开的光学假象，再扩展为任何越走近越落空的虚假希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shining sheet of water on the road that vanishes at a touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上那片一闪一闪的水，一走近就消失。

branches.en: The physical image made by hot air is the base sense.
branches.cn: 热空气造成的水影与远景，是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: A hope that keeps retreating is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 越追越远的希望，是这个词的比喻义项。

branches.en: Light bending above hot sand is the science behind the image.
branches.cn: 热沙上方的空气使光线偏折，是这个影像背后的物理原理。

branches.en: A mirage of water and a mirage of wealth both invite pursuit and then dissolve.
branches.cn: 水影与财富的幻影都会引人追逐，随后消散。

branches.en: The false hope is the image seen at a distance and mistaken for a promise.
branches.cn: 虚假的希望就是远处那幅被误当成承诺的影子。

intro.en: Mirage is a French noun in -age built on the verb mirer, which comes from Latin mirari, to wonder at, and it arrived in English as a loan word.
intro.cn: mirage 是法语里以 -age 结尾、由动词 mirer 构成的名词，mirer 又来自拉丁语 mirari（惊奇地看），这个词是以借词身份进入英语的。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari means to wonder at, mirus means wonderful, and miror is the verb used in the older spelling of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mirari 意为「惊奇地看」，mirus 意为「奇妙的」，miror 是这个词族的动词形式。

items.example: The root mir- appears in mirror, admire, and miracle.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mir- 出现在 mirror、admire 与 miracle 里。

items.example: Mirari is the source of the French verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: mirari 是这个名词背后那个法语动词的源头。

items.example: Mirus is the adjective behind miracle.
items.exampleCN: mirus 是 miracle 背后的形容词。

items.meaning: to look at oneself in a mirror
items.example: Se mirer gives the noun mirage directly.
items.exampleCN: se mirer 直接构成了名词 mirage。

items.meaning: an action, process, or its result
items.meaningCN: 表示动作、过程或其结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -age turns se mirer into the noun mirage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 把 se mirer 变成名词 mirage。

items.example: Mirror keeps the concrete look-in-a-glass sense.
items.exampleCN: mirror 保留了「照看玻璃」的具体含义。

items.meaning: to look at with respect and pleasure
items.example: Admire adds ad- to mirari, meaning to look towards.
items.exampleCN: admire 在 mirari 前加了 ad-，表示「朝……看」。

items.example: Miracle keeps the sense of wonder in the family.
items.exampleCN: miracle 保留了这个词族里「惊奇」的意味。

definition_zh: 欢笑；笑声；快乐；欢欣；（带几分贬义的）哄笑
definition_en: a feeling of cheerful and noisy laughter, often seen as light or even foolish by others
core_image: 满屋人笑得前仰后合，笑声从敞开的窗子淌到街上
scene: 婚宴上，新郎被亲友们说的笑话逗得笑个不停，满厅都是笑声。The wedding hall rang with mirth as the bride told a story about their first meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 mirth 是「欢笑；笑声」（第 1 个义项：响亮而愉快的笑声或笑闹）；句意：新娘讲起两人第一次见面的故事时，婚宴大厅里充满了欢笑。

pos.zh: 哄笑；取乐（常带贬义，指拿别人的窘境当乐子）

derivatives.zh: mirth + -ful，义为「欢快的；充满笑声的」
mirth + -less，义为「毫无笑意的；干巴巴的」
mirthless + -ly，义为「毫无笑意地」
与 mirth 同出古英语词根 myrgth（快乐），义为「欢乐的；快活的」

senses.title: Noisy cheerful laughter
senses.definition: happiness that shows itself in loud, cheerful laughter shared by a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一群人响亮而愉快地笑出来的快乐
senses.example: Her jokes filled the room with mirth.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑话让整个房间充满了欢笑。
senses.why: Old English myrgth comes from the root of merry and means joy, so the word began as plain joy that is heard as laughter.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 myrgth 出自 merry（欢乐）的词根，本义就是「快乐」，而这种快乐是能被听见的，于是它专指笑出来的欢快，核心画面是满屋的笑声。

senses.title: Laughter felt to be foolish
senses.definition: loud laughter that seems light, foolish, or unfeeling to the people who hear it
senses.definitionCN: 在旁人听来显得轻浮、愚蠢或缺乏同情心的哄笑
senses.example: There was a hint of mirth in the crowd when the speaker tripped.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者绊了一下时，人群里透出一丝幸灾乐祸的笑声。
senses.why: The same bright laughter can sound unkind when it is aimed at someone else, so the word also carries a frown from outside the group.
senses.whyCN: 同样是明亮的笑声，一旦冲着别人的窘态发出，听在外人耳里就成了不厚道的哄笑，所以这个词也带着旁观者皱眉的那一层。

intro.en: Mirth goes back to Old English myrgth or mirhth, joy and pleasure, built from the same Germanic root as merry.
intro.cn: mirth 可追溯到古英语 myrgth（也写作 mirhth），意为「快乐、愉悦」，与 merry 同出日耳曼语词根。

items.en: A root meaning short and merry, reconstructed as murgjaz, lies behind the family.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词族背后有一个意为「短暂而愉快」的日耳曼语词根，重构形式常写作 murgjaz。

items.en: Myrgth and mirhth name joy, pleasure, and gladness in Old English.
items.cn: 古英语 myrgth 与 mirhth 表示快乐、愉悦与高兴。

items.en: The spelling settles towards mirth, and the sense narrows to laughter that can be heard.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 mirth，词义收窄到「能被听见的笑」。

items.en: Writers pair mirth with folly and excess, giving the word its gently critical edge.
items.cn: 十六世纪的作者常把 mirth 与愚妄、放纵并提，于是这个词带上了一点批评的意味。

items.en: Mirth survives mainly in literary and formal writing, while merry keeps the everyday ground.
items.cn: 现代英语里 mirth 主要用于文学与正式文体，日常场景多由 merry 承担。

note.en: Mirth belongs to the Germanic merry family, with merry, mirthful, and mirthless, and it stands near words for laughter and joy.
note.cn: mirth 属于日耳曼语系「欢乐」词族，与 merry、mirthful、mirthless 同源；在意义上与表示笑与快乐的词相邻，但强调「笑出声」。

entries.definition: happy and lively, especially in company
full of laughter and cheer
without any real laughter or joy
the time when a baby is born
entries.definitionCN: 出生，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the sound or act of laughing
great delight, sometimes at another person misfortune
loud and uncontrolled laughter in a group

normalIntro.en: Mirth comes from the same Old English family as merry, so the two words share the sound of laughter held in the throat.
normalIntro.cn: mirth 与 merry 同出古英语词族，两者都带着笑声缩在喉咙里的声音感。

normal.en: Old English myrgth is the ancestor of mirth and also of merry, so both words carry the same joy.
normal.cn: 古英语 myrgth 既是 mirth 的祖先，也与 merry 同源，所以两个词共享同一份快乐。

normal.en: The noun suffix -th builds abstract nouns from adjectives, as in warmth from warm and depth from deep.
normal.cn: 名词词尾 -th 把形容词变成抽象名词，如 warm 变 warmth、deep 变 depth。

normal.en: The suffix -ful in mirthful means full of, while -less in mirthless means without.
normal.cn: mirthful 里的 -ful 表示「充满」，mirthless 里的 -less 表示「没有」，正好是一对。

normal.en: Formal writing has fixed phrases such as with mirth and a roar of mirth.
normal.cn: 正式文体里有固定说法：with mirth（带着笑意）与 a roar of mirth（一阵哄堂大笑）。

normal.en: Compare merry and mirth: merry describes the mood, mirth names the sound it makes.
normal.cn: 对比 merry 与 mirth：merry 描写心情，mirth 指这种心情发出的声音。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded room bursting into laughter at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋的人在同一瞬间爆出笑声。

abstract.en: Think of laughter spilling out through an open window into the street.
abstract.cn: 想象笑声从敞开的窗子涌到街上。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher frowning at a class that keeps giggling at the wrong time.
abstract.cn: 想象老师皱着眉，看着全班在不该笑的时候笑个不停。

examples.en: The old friends met again, and the table was full of mirth all evening.
examples.cn: 老朋友们重聚，整晚桌上都充满着欢笑。

examples.en: His quiet, mirthless smile told us the news was serious.
examples.cn: 他那毫无笑意的微笑告诉我们，消息很严重。

examples.en: There is little mirth in a village that has lost its harvest.
examples.cn: 一个失去收成的村子里，很少有什么欢笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妹 儿 笑」——妹妹一笑，满屋欢笑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 日耳曼语词根 murgjaz（短暂而愉快，重构形式）→ 古英语 myrgth（快乐）→ 中古英语 mirth → 现代英语 mirth，核心义「听得见的欢乐」。

sensesIntro.en: Mirth begins as plain joy heard as laughter, then takes on a slight edge when outsiders see the laughter as foolish or unkind.
sensesIntro.cn: mirth 先是被听见的、单纯的快乐，后来在旁观者眼里显得轻浮或不厚道时，又多了一层带着批评的意味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of people laughing so hard that the walls seem to shake.
core.cn: 核心意象：满屋人笑得墙都快晃起来。

branches.en: Cheerful shared laughter is the base sense.
branches.cn: 大家一起欢快地笑，是这个词的基础义项。

branches.en: Laughter that seems foolish from outside is the critical sense.
branches.cn: 在旁人看来显得愚蠢的笑，是这个词的批评义项。

branches.en: The everyday counterpart merry carries the same joy in adjective form.
branches.cn: 日常用的 merry 以形容词形式承载着同一份欢乐。

branches.en: The same laugh can warm the room or sting the person it is aimed at.
branches.cn: 同一种笑，既能暖场，也能刺伤被笑的人。

branches.en: The mirthless smile is the word turned inside out, laughter without joy.
branches.cn: mirthless 的干笑正是这个词的反面：有笑的外形，没有快乐的内核。

intro.en: Mirth is an Old English noun in -th built on the adjective stem that also gives merry, and English offers both a full and an empty version with -ful and -less.
intro.cn: mirth 是以 -th 结尾的古英语名词，词干同时给出 merry；英语又用 -ful 和 -less 造出「有笑」与「无笑」两个版本。

latinIntro.en: Mirth is a Germanic word and has no Latin ancestors, so the family is of English and Norse rather than of Latin origin.
latinIntro.cn: mirth 是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语祖先，所以这个词族来自英语与北欧语的源头，而非拉丁语。

items.example: Myrgth is the Old English noun that becomes mirth.
items.exampleCN: myrgth 是变成 mirth 的古英语名词。

items.example: Merry shares its root with mirth.
items.exampleCN: merry 与 mirth 共享词根。

items.meaning: forms a noun of state from an adjective
items.meaningCN: 把形容词变为状态名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -th is also seen in warmth and depth.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -th 也见于 warmth 与 depth。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms mirthful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 mirthful。

items.example: The suffix -less forms mirthless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 mirthless。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mirthlessly and mirthfully.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 mirthlessly 与 mirthfully。

items.example: Laughter is the everyday word that mirth dresses up.
items.exampleCN: laughter 是 mirth 在日常里的通俗说法。

items.example: Glee is close to mirth in its joyful edge.
items.exampleCN: glee 与 mirth 在欢快这一点上很接近。

items.meaning: a feeling of happiness or encouragement
items.example: Cheer is a formal cousin of mirth.
items.exampleCN: cheer 是 mirth 的正式近亲。

definition_zh: 各色混杂的；各种各样的；杂项类的
definition_en: consisting of many different kinds of things that do not form a single group
core_image: 一只手提箱倒扣在地上，亮面徽章、毛线团、小钥匙撒成一堆，每样东西都不同类
scene: 搬家工人把最后一箱东西倒扣下来，徽章、旧票据和几件工具混在一处，谁也说不清它们算什么。 We packed the miscellaneous items into a box labelled odds and ends.
sceneCN: 这里 miscellaneous 是「各色混杂的」（第 1 个义项：种类互不相同而又被放进同一处）；句意：我们把那些杂七杂八的东西装进一个写着「零碎物件」的箱子。

pos.zh: 各色混杂的；各种各样的
杂项类的；其它未分类的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词名词化而来，义为「杂集；杂录」
拉丁语复数形式借入英语，义为「杂录；杂项」
形容词加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「混杂状态」
形容词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「混杂地；杂项地」

senses.title: Made up of mixed kinds
senses.definition: containing many different kinds of things that do not match one another
senses.definitionCN: 包含许多种类不同、彼此并不相配的东西
senses.example: The shelf held a miscellaneous collection of seashells, buttons and coins.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上放着一堆杂七杂八的收藏：贝壳、纽扣和硬币。
senses.why: The Latin source miscellus means mixed, so the adjective first names a heap whose parts have no shared kind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 miscellus 意为「混合的」，所以这个形容词最初指的是一堆彼此没有共同类别的东西。

senses.title: Belonging to the leftover category
senses.definition: used to label things that do not fit any main group, on lists, forms or accounts
senses.definitionCN: 在清单、表格或账目上用来标记无法归入任何主要类别的东西
senses.example: Fill in the fields marked name, date and miscellaneous.
senses.exampleCN: 请填写姓名、日期和杂项这几栏。
senses.why: Once a heap has no kind of its own, it becomes the label for the last box, the leftovers that no list category covers.
senses.whyCN: 一堆东西一旦没有自己的类别，就会变成最后那个格子的标签，用来装清单上别的类目都装不下的剩余物。

senses.title: Varied in writing or style
senses.definition: describing a published collection that mixes essays, notes, poems or fragments
senses.definitionCN: 形容把随笔、笔记、诗歌或片段混合在一起的出版物
senses.example: The magazine is a miscellany of short pieces on travel, food and art.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志是旅行、美食与艺术短文的杂集。
senses.why: A book can also be a heap: mixed contents become a popular publishing genre from the sixteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 一本书也可以是一堆杂物：自十六世纪起，混杂的内容成了一种受欢迎的出版体裁。

senses.title: Minor and varied in accounts
senses.definition: describing small sums that are spread over many different purposes
senses.definitionCN: 形容分散在许多不同用途上的小额款项
senses.example: Miscellaneous expenses such as postage and printing came to forty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 邮资、印刷等杂项开支合计四十英镑。
senses.why: Accounting takes the leftover category and names every small, unrelated cost with it.
senses.whyCN: 会计沿用「剩余类别」这一用法，把每一笔小额又不相关的支出都归到它名下。

senses.title: Groups that do not combine
senses.definition: describing a crowd or company of people of very different kinds
senses.definitionCN: 形容由完全不同类别的人组成的群体
senses.example: A miscellaneous crowd of tourists, traders and officers pushed through the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群游客、商人和军官混杂着挤过大门。
senses.why: People, too, can be a heap: the adjective reaches from objects to crowds who share no rank or trade.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以成为一堆：这个形容词从物件延伸到彼此没有共同身份或行业的人群。

intro.en: Miscellaneous goes back to the Latin verb miscere, to mix, through the adjective miscellus, meaning mixed, and then miscellaneus.
intro.cn: miscellaneous 源自拉丁语动词 miscere（混合），经形容词 miscellus（混合的）、miscellaneus 演变而来。

items.en: Miscere means to mix or mingle.
items.cn: miscere 意为混合、掺和。

items.en: Miscellus, meaning mixed, is a small or altered form of miscere.
items.cn: miscellus 意为「混合的」，是 miscere 的指小或变形形式。

items.en: Miscellaneus means mixed or of mixed kinds.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 miscellaneus 意为「混合的、杂类的」。

items.en: English borrows miscellany first, the noun for a mixed collection.
items.cn: 英语先借入名词 miscellany，指混合的汇集或杂集。

items.en: The adjective miscellaneous appears, describing mixed groups of things.
items.cn: 形容词 miscellaneous 出现，用来形容混杂在一起的东西。

items.en: Printing, accounting and form design turn it into the standard leftover label.
items.cn: 印刷、会计与表格设计把它变成标准的「杂项」标签。

note.en: Miscellaneous shares the Latin mixing root with miscellany and is close to everyday words such as various and assorted.
note.cn: miscellaneous 与 miscellany 共享拉丁语「混合」词根，并与 various、assorted 等日常词义近。

entries.definition: a mixed collection of things or writings
a collection of miscellaneous items, especially writings
in a mixed or unclassified way
of several different kinds
of various sorts put together
a mixed group of many kinds of things
entries.definitionCN: 同族名词，意为「各类混杂的一组」

normalIntro.en: Miscellaneous is a heap of mixed things, and its family nodes miscellany and miscellanea all start with mis-.
normalIntro.cn: miscellaneous 是一堆混在一起的东西，同族的 miscellany 与 miscellanea 都以 mis- 开头。

normal.en: Miscellaneous items are odds and ends with no common kind.
normal.cn: miscellaneous items 就是没有共同类别的零碎物件。

normal.en: A miscellaneous collection is a jar of stamps, shells, buttons and coins.
normal.cn: a miscellaneous collection 就是一罐邮票、贝壳、纽扣和硬币。

normal.en: In accounting, miscellaneous expenses are small costs for many different things.
normal.cn: 在会计里，miscellaneous expenses 指用途各异的零星开销。

normal.en: Compare miscellany: the noun names the book or pile, the adjective describes how mixed it is.
normal.cn: 对比 miscellany：名词指那本书或那堆东西本身，形容词说明它有多混杂。

normal.en: Spell the double s before cells: misc + ellaneous, as if the cells are mixed together.
normal.cn: 拼写时注意 cells 前有两个 s：misc 加 ellaneous，像是许多格子混在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer tipped upside down on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉翻倒在地上。

abstract.en: Think of the last box on a form, marked with three dots.
abstract.cn: 想象表格最末一格，只写了三个点。

abstract.en: See a magazine whose pages jump from travel to recipes to poems.
abstract.cn: 想象一本杂志，页面从旅行跳到菜谱再跳到诗歌。

examples.en: Drawers full of miscellaneous papers had to be sorted first.
examples.cn: 塞满杂七杂八文件的抽屉得先整理。

examples.en: The contract has a clause about miscellaneous fees.
examples.cn: 合同里有一条规定杂项费用的条款。

examples.en: Her bag was a miscellaneous mix of receipts, pens and foreign coins.
examples.cn: 她的包里杂乱地混着收据、笔和外国硬币。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米散」——米袋破了，白米撒成一地，什么都有混在一起；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 miscere（混合）→ miscellus（混合的）→ 晚期拉丁语 miscellaneus → 英语 miscellaneous，词根义为「混在一起」。

sensesIntro.en: Miscellaneous starts from mixed contents, then moves to the leftover label on lists, to mixed publications, to small varied sums, and finally to mixed crowds.
sensesIntro.cn: miscellaneous 从混杂的内容出发，进而指清单上的杂项标签、体裁混杂的出版物、零星杂费，最后指品流混杂的人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tipped box whose contents are every different kind at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：翻倒的箱子，里面的东西品类各不相同。

branches.en: MIXING: the adjective describes a heap whose parts share no kind.
branches.cn: 混合线：形容词描述一堆没有共同类别的东西。

branches.en: LABELLING: the heap becomes the last category on a list.
branches.cn: 标签线：那堆东西变成清单上最后一类。

branches.en: PUBLISHING: mixed writings become a recognised genre.
branches.cn: 出版线：混杂的文章成为一种被认可的体裁。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS: small unrelated sums take the same leftover label.
branches.cn: 账目线：互不相关的小额款项沿用同一个「剩余」标签。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a crowd of different trades and ranks can be a heap too.
branches.cn: 人群线：行业与身份不同的人群也可以算作一堆。

intro.en: Miscellaneous is built from the Latin mixing root misce- plus the adjective endings -llaneus and -eous.
intro.cn: miscellaneous 由拉丁语「混合」词根 misce- 加形容词词尾 -llaneus、-eous 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin miscere means to mix; its derivatives miscellus and miscellaneus carry the same mixed idea into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 miscere 意为混合；它的派生形式 miscellus 与 miscellaneus 把同样的「混杂」之意带入英语。

items.example: Miscere is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: miscere 是整族词的词根。

items.example: Miscellus shrinks miscere into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: miscellus 把 miscere 变成一个描述词。

items.example: Miscellaneus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: miscellaneus 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: A miscellany names the pile itself.
items.exampleCN: miscellany 指那堆东西本身。

items.example: Miscellanea keeps the Latin plural ending.
items.exampleCN: miscellanea 保留了拉丁语复数词尾。

items.example: The suffix -aneous appears as -eous in miscellaneous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -aneous 在 miscellaneous 中表现为 -eous。

items.example: Miscellaneous is the standard adjective today.
items.exampleCN: miscellaneous 是今天通用的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb miscellaneously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 miscellaneously。

items.example: The suffix -ness names the mixed state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 表示混杂的状态。

definition_zh: 淘气的；调皮的；恶作剧的；有害的
definition_en: showing a fondness for playful tricks that annoy or mildly harm others, or causing damage
core_image: 一个孩子躲在门后，手里藏着小纸团，眼睛弯弯地准备恶作剧
scene: 糖果罐被挪到了柜顶，而站在角落里的小人儿却冲你眨了眨眼，一脸得意。 The mischievous child hid the teacher chalk in a cupboard.
sceneCN: 这里 mischievous 是「调皮恶作剧的」（第 2 个义项：喜欢开玩笑、给他人添点小麻烦）；句意：那个调皮的孩子把老师的粉笔藏进了柜子里。

pos.zh: 淘气的；调皮的；爱恶作剧的

derivatives.zh: 词根词，义为「恶作剧；淘气；损害」
形容词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「调皮地；恶作剧地」
形容词加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「调皮；淘气」
基础名词，义为「恶作剧；祸害」，与形容词同源

senses.title: Fond of playful tricks
senses.titleCN: 爱闹着玩的；爱恶作剧的
senses.definition: enjoying tricks and jokes that gently tease other people
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢拿别人打趣的恶作剧和小玩笑
senses.example: He has a mischievous sense of humour that keeps the staffroom lively.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一种爱恶作剧的幽默感，让办公室里总是很热闹。
senses.why: The Old French word meschief meant a bad outcome or misfortune, and its adjective shifted to a person who enjoys causing small trouble.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 meschief 意为「不幸的结果」，其形容词后来转向指喜欢惹点小麻烦的人。

senses.title: Playfully naughty in behaviour
senses.definition: describing children or animals that are naughty in a playful way
senses.definitionCN: 形容孩子或动物以玩闹的方式不听话
senses.example: The mischievous child hid the teacher chalk in a cupboard.
senses.exampleCN: 那个调皮的孩子把老师的粉笔藏进了自己的靴子里。
senses.why: Small harm is the heart of the word, so its modern tone is often fond rather than harsh.
senses.whyCN: 「小祸害」是这个词的内核，所以现代语气常常是亲昵的，而不是严厉指责。

senses.title: Happening by bad luck
senses.definition: old and literary use describing an unlucky or unfortunate thing
senses.definitionCN: 古旧而带文学色彩，表示运气不好、不幸
senses.example: The mischievous wind had torn the sail before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那阵倒霉的风在天亮前撕破了船帆。
senses.why: Short for mischievous fortune, the adjective once meant having the bad luck of meschief.
senses.whyCN: 它本是 mischievous fortune 的省略形式，曾表示遭遇 meschief 那种厄运。

senses.title: Actively harmful
senses.definition: formal use describing something that causes real damage or harm
senses.definitionCN: 正式用语，指造成实际损害的东西
senses.example: Mischievous rumours can damage a young person reputation for years.
senses.exampleCN: 恶意的谣言能在很多年里毁掉一个年轻人的名声。
senses.why: The older meaning of real harm survives in formal writing about damage.
senses.whyCN: 「真正的祸害」这一旧义，仍旧保留在讨论损害的正式文章里。

intro.en: Mischievous comes from the Old French noun meschief, meaning misfortune or harm, which became the English noun mischief, plus the adjective ending -ous.
intro.cn: mischievous 来自古法语名词 meschief（不幸、祸害），它演变成英语名词 mischief，再加形容词词尾 -ous。

items.en: Meschief comes from meschever, to come to harm, built from mes-, poorly, and chief, head or end.
items.cn: meschief 源于 meschever（遭殃），由 mes-（不好）与 chief（头、结局）构成。

items.en: The noun mischief appears, meaning harm or misfortune.
items.cn: 英语中出现名词 mischief，意为损害或不幸。

items.en: Mischievous forms from mischief with the suffix -ous, meaning harmful.
items.cn: mischief 加词尾 -ous 构成 mischievous，意为有害的。

items.en: The sense moves from causing harm to being playfully naughty.
items.cn: 词义从「造成损害」转向「顽皮淘气」。

items.en: Expressions such as mischievous fortune keep the older unlucky use alive.
items.cn: mischievous fortune 这类说法让旧的「倒霉」之义留存下来。

items.en: Everyday speech now favours the playful sense, while formal writing keeps the harmful one.
items.cn: 现代英语日常多用顽皮之义，正式文体仍保留有害之义。

note.en: Mischievous belongs to the mis- family with mischief and mischief maker, and sits near playful words such as naughty and roguish.
note.cn: mischievous 属于以 mis- 开头的 mischief 词族，并与 naughty、roguish 等「顽皮」词义近。

entries.definition: playful bad behaviour, or harm
in a playful, teasing way
a person who likes causing playful trouble
entries.definitionCN: 爱惹麻烦、爱恶作剧的人

entries.definition: badly behaved, often in a playful way
playfully dishonest or charmingly tricky
given to playing practical jokes

normalIntro.en: Mischievous is the adjective of mischief, and the noun itself once meant a bad outcome from the Old French verb meschever.
normalIntro.cn: mischievous 是 mischief 的形容词，而这个名词原本指古法语动词 meschever 带来的坏结局。

normal.en: A mischievous grin shows a plan for a harmless trick.
normal.cn: a mischievous grin 是准备搞个无伤大雅恶作剧的笑。

normal.en: Mischievous rumours cause real harm, so try to avoid this word for playful things.
normal.cn: mischievous rumours 会造成真实伤害，所以别用这个词形容轻松的玩闹。

normal.en: Compare mischief: the noun is the trouble, the adjective describes the person who makes it.
normal.cn: 对比 mischief：名词指麻烦本身，形容词描述制造麻烦的人。

normal.en: Keep the i after the ch: mischief plus ous gives mischievous, not mischevious.
normal.cn: 注意 ch 后保留 i：mischief 加 ous 得 mischievous，而不是 mischevious。

normal.en: Say mish-chuh-vus with three syllables, not four.
normal.cn: 读作 mish-chuh-vus，共三个音节，不要读成四个音节。

abstract.en: Imagine a child holding a whoopee cushion behind the back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子把坐垫藏在身后。

abstract.en: Picture eyes that curve up right before a small trick.
abstract.cn: 想象搞小把戏前弯成月牙的眼睛。

abstract.en: See a wind that sinks a toy boat while the children laugh.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵风把玩具船吹翻，孩子们却在笑。

examples.en: She gave him a mischievous smile and said nothing.
examples.cn: 她冲他调皮地一笑，什么也没说。

examples.en: The mischievous puppy chewed every pair of shoes.
examples.cn: 那只调皮的小狗把每一双鞋都咬了。

examples.en: His comment was mischievous rather than cruel.
examples.cn: 他的评论只是调皮，并非恶意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米什切沃斯」——听到切声就知道有人在偷偷搞小动作；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 meschever（遭殃，mes- 不 + chief 结局）→ meschief（不幸、祸害）→ 中古英语 mischief → mischief 加 -ous 成为 mischievous，核心义「惹出小祸」。

sensesIntro.en: Mischievous runs from a taste for playful tricks to naughty behaviour, to its old sense of bad luck, and finally to real harm in formal use.
sensesIntro.cn: mischievous 从喜欢玩闹恶作剧，到实际的顽皮举止，再到古老的「倒霉」之义，最后在正式用法中指真正的损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child hiding a crumpled paper ball behind the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子把揉好的纸团藏在门后。

branches.en: HUMOUR: enjoying tricks is the mildest modern sense.
branches.cn: 幽默线：喜欢恶作剧是今天最温和的义项。

branches.en: CHILDREN: the playful child is the word at its most familiar.
branches.cn: 孩童线：顽皮的孩子是这个词最常见的形象。

branches.en: BAD LUCK: the old meschief sense survives in literary use.
branches.cn: 厄运线：古老的 meschief 之义仍见于文学用法。

branches.en: HARM: formal writing keeps the meaning of real damage.
branches.cn: 损害线：正式文体保留真实伤害的含义。

branches.en: The same word covers a harmless prank and a harmful rumour.
branches.cn: 同词线：同一个词既指无害的玩笑，也指有害的谣言。

intro.en: Mischievous is mischief with the Latin suffix -ous, meaning full of, and its family is rooted in Old French chief, head or end.
intro.cn: mischievous 是 mischief 加拉丁语词尾 -ous（充满……的），整个词族根植于古法语 chief（头、结局）。

latinIntro.en: The root is Old French rather than Latin, but the adjective ending -ous comes from Latin -osus, so the family has a hybrid history.
latinIntro.cn: 词根本身是古法语而非拉丁语，但形容词词尾 -ous 来自拉丁语 -osus，所以这个词族是混合来源。

items.example: Mischief is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: mischief 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Meschief is the French source.
items.exampleCN: meschief 是法语来源。

items.example: Meschever is built from mes- and chief.
items.exampleCN: meschever 由 mes- 与 chief 构成。

items.example: The prefix mes- adds a negative twist.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mes- 加上负面转折。

items.example: The suffix -ous turns mischief into mischievous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把 mischief 变成 mischievous。

items.example: Mischievous keeps the French spelling of chief.
items.exampleCN: mischievous 保留了 chief 的法语拼写。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb mischievously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 mischievously。

items.meaning: a person who stirs up trouble
items.example: Mischief maker joins the noun with maker.
items.exampleCN: mischief maker 是名词与 maker 的组合。

definition_zh: 不幸；厄运；灾祸；不幸的事
definition_en: bad luck, or an unlucky event that brings suffering
core_image: 刚刚还握着好签的手，突然被一阵风吹掉了签纸，只剩空空的掌心
scene: 船队在海峡里遇上连日暴风，返航时只剩一只小船，白发船长始终不愿说出家里出了事。 The family never recovered from the misfortune of losing their farm.
sceneCN: 这里 misfortune 是「不幸的遭遇」（第 2 个义项：造成痛苦的坏事或灾祸）；句意：这家人始终没有从失去农场的这场不幸中恢复过来。

pos.zh: 不幸；厄运；灾祸；不幸的事

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「幸运的」
基础词，义为「运气；财富」
同根形容词，义为「偶然的」
前缀 un- 加 fortunate，义为「不幸的」

senses.title: Bad luck
senses.definition: the state of being unlucky rather than being at fault
senses.definitionCN: 不走运的状态，而不是自己的过错
senses.example: He blamed misfortune for the loss of his shop, not laziness.
senses.exampleCN: 他把店铺倒闭归咎于厄运，而不是懒惰。
senses.why: Misfortune is fortune with the Old French prefix mis-, meaning bad, so it names bad luck itself, not a fault.
senses.whyCN: misfortune 是 fortune 加古法语前缀 mis-（坏的），所以它指坏运气本身，而不指过失。

senses.title: An unlucky event
senses.definition: a single unlucky event that brings loss or suffering
senses.definitionCN: 带来损失或痛苦的一件倒霉事
senses.example: The flood was the first misfortune that year.
senses.exampleCN: 洪灾是那年的第一场不幸。
senses.why: Once bad luck can be counted, the noun turns plural and names each single disaster.
senses.whyCN: 厄运一旦可以被数出来，这个名词就会变成复数，指一件件具体的灾祸。

senses.title: Pity for someone
senses.definition: a person or thing that deserves pity
senses.definitionCN: 值得同情的人或事物
senses.example: The old clerk was a true misfortune of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老职员真是小镇上令人怜悯的不幸之人。
senses.why: Old use treats the sufferer as a misfortune too, shifting the word onto the person who meets it.
senses.whyCN: 古旧用法把承受者也看作一种 misfortune，于是这个词转到了遭遇不幸的人身上。

senses.title: Bad luck seen as a force
senses.definition: an impersonal force that keeps bringing bad events
senses.definitionCN: 不断带来坏事的无形的力量
senses.example: Misfortune seemed to follow the brothers across three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 厄运似乎跟着那几兄弟走了三个国家。
senses.why: Like fortune, the word can be personified, so bad luck becomes a power that follows people.
senses.whyCN: 与 fortune 一样，这个词也可以被拟人化，于是坏运气变成一种追着人跑的力量。

intro.en: Misfortune is the Latin-derived fortune, through Old French, with the Old French prefix mis-, meaning bad or ill.
intro.cn: misfortune 是来自拉丁语、经古法语进入英语的 fortune，加上古法语前缀 mis-（坏的）构成。

items.en: Fortuna is the Roman goddess of luck, from fors, meaning chance.
items.cn: fortuna 是罗马幸运女神，源自 fors（偶然、机会）。

items.en: Fortune reaches Old French as both luck and wealth.
items.cn: fortune 进入古法语，兼指运气与财富。

items.en: English borrows fortune from French, meaning chance or fate.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入 fortune，意为机遇或命运。

items.en: Old French mis- marks something bad, so misfortune is literally bad fortune.
items.cn: 古法语前缀 mis- 表示「坏的」，所以 misfortune 字面即「坏运气」。

items.en: Misfortune appears in English for bad luck and for an unlucky event.
items.cn: 英语中出现了 misfortune，兼指厄运与不幸的事件。

items.en: The plural misfortunes names separate disasters, while the singular stays abstract.
items.cn: 复数 misfortunes 指一次次具体的灾祸，单数仍是抽象的不幸。

note.en: Misfortune is the mis- form of fortune and sits near disaster, adversity and bad luck words.
note.cn: misfortune 是 fortune 的 mis- 形式，与 disaster、adversity 等「灾祸」词义近。

entries.definition: luck, or a large amount of money
lucky
unlucky, or regrettable
a sudden event that causes great damage
difficult or unlucky conditions
a small unlucky accident

normalIntro.en: Misfortune is simply bad fortune, and its neighbours fortunate, unfortunate and fortuitous all share the Latin fors, chance.
normalIntro.cn: misfortune 就是「坏的 fortune」，其同族 fortunate、unfortunate、fortuitous 都共享拉丁语 fors（偶然）。

normal.en: Have the misfortune to do something means being unlucky enough to do it.
normal.cn: 「have the misfortune to do」表示不幸地做了某事。

normal.en: A misfortune is a single bad event, misfortunes are many of them.
normal.cn: a misfortune 是一件坏事，misfortunes 是许多件。

normal.en: A companion in misfortune is someone who shares the bad luck.
normal.cn: a companion in misfortune 指患难与共的人。

normal.en: Compare unfortunate: the adjective describes the person, the noun names the bad luck itself.
normal.cn: 对比 unfortunate：形容词描述人，名词指坏运气本身。

normal.en: The mis- prefix means badly, so misfortune is the opposite of good fortune.
normal.cn: 前缀 mis- 表示「坏」，所以 misfortune 是好运的反面。

abstract.en: Picture a wind that blows the winning ticket out of the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵风吹走了手里中奖的票。

abstract.en: See a black cat walking slowly across the road twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一只黑猫慢慢走过马路两次。

abstract.en: Think of a coin flipping to the same side again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币一次次翻到同一面。

examples.en: He bore his misfortune with quiet courage.
examples.cn: 他以平静的勇气承受自己的不幸。

examples.en: The storm was just the latest misfortune to hit the village.
examples.cn: 这场风暴不过是袭击村庄的又一次不幸。

examples.en: She had the misfortune to arrive on the day of the strike.
examples.cn: 她不幸赶上罢工那天到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「觅斯福琼」——想找福气却总是落空，便是厄运；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fors（偶然、机缘）→ 幸运女神 Fortuna → fortuna（运气）→ 古法语 fortune → 英语 fortune 加前缀 mis-（坏的）→ misfortune，核心义「坏运气」。

sensesIntro.en: Misfortune covers bad luck as a state, each counted unlucky event, the pitied sufferer in old use, and bad luck pictured as a force.
sensesIntro.cn: misfortune 涵盖作为状态的不幸、一件件被数出来的倒霉事、古旧用法中值得怜悯的人，以及被拟人化的厄运。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gust of wind lifts the lucky slip out of an open hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵风把写着好运的纸条吹离摊开的手掌。

branches.en: STATE: bad luck as a condition, opposite of good fortune.
branches.cn: 状态线：作为境况的坏运气，是好运的反面。

branches.en: EVENT: each counted unlucky event becomes a misfortune in the plural.
branches.cn: 事件线：被一件件数出来的倒霉事，复数即 misfortunes。

branches.en: PERSON: old use moves the word onto the one who suffers.
branches.cn: 人物线：古旧用法把词义转到承受者身上。

branches.en: FORCE: personified like fortune, it follows people across countries.
branches.cn: 力量线：像 fortune 一样被拟人化，跟着人跨过国界。

branches.en: the abstract state of bad luck and each concrete unlucky event feed one another.
branches.cn: 抽象状态与具体事件共用同一份坏运气。

intro.en: Misfortune joins the Old French prefix mis-, meaning bad, to fortune, which comes from Latin fors, chance.
intro.cn: misfortune 把古法语前缀 mis-（坏的）加在 fortune 上，而 fortune 源自拉丁语 fors（偶然）。

latinIntro.en: Latin fors and fortuna lie behind fortune; the mis- part comes from Old French, so the origins of this word are mixed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fors 与 fortuna 是 fortune 的来源，而 mis- 来自古法语，因此词源是混合的。

items.example: Fors is the deep root of fortune.
items.exampleCN: fors 是 fortune 的深层词根。

items.example: Fortuna gave English fortune.
items.exampleCN: fortuna 演变为英语 fortune。

items.example: Fortune is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: fortune 是基础名词。

items.example: The prefix mis- reverses the luck.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mis- 把运气反转。

items.example: Misfortune is bad fortune in one word.
items.exampleCN: misfortune 就是写在一个词里的坏运气。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms fortunate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 fortunate。

items.example: The prefix un- builds unfortunate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unfortunate。

items.example: Fortuitous keeps the chance sense.
items.exampleCN: fortuitous 保留了偶然之义。

items.example: The plural counts separate misfortunes.
items.exampleCN: 复数指点明一次次分开的不幸。

definition_zh: 处理不当；粗暴对待；应对失当；（运动）接球失误
definition_en: to deal with something in the wrong way, or to hold and use it roughly, so that it goes wrong badly
core_image: 一双手没抓稳，东西在掌心里一歪，掉在地上发出闷响
scene: 快递员把纸箱随手一摔，里面的玻璃罐全碎了。The courier mishandled the parcel, and the glass jars inside were all broken.
sceneCN: 这里 mishandle 是「处理不当；弄得不好」（第 1 个义项：因方式不对而把事情办坏或把东西弄坏）；句意：快递员把包裹处置失当，里面的玻璃罐全碎了。

pos.zh: 处理不当；粗暴对待；应对失当；（运动）接球失误

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 名词化，表示「处理不当；粗暴对待」的行为
handle 加 -er 表示做事的人，义为「操作者；搬运工」
mishandle 的基础词，义为「处理；拿握」
handle 加 -ing 构成，义为「处理；搬运」

senses.title: To deal with something badly
senses.definition: to deal with a task, case, or piece of business badly, so that things go wrong
senses.definitionCN: 把任务、案件或事情办得不好，使事情出错
senses.example: The company mishandled the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把投诉处理得很糟。
senses.why: The prefix mis- reverses the good sense of handle, so handling becomes the wrong kind of handling.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 mis- 把 handle「处理得当」的意思反转，于是「处理」变成了「弄糟」。

senses.title: To hold or use roughly
senses.definition: to hold, move, or use an object in a careless and rough way
senses.definitionCN: 漫不经心又粗暴地拿、搬或使用某物
senses.example: He mishandled the fragile vase.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那只易碎的花瓶粗暴地搬来搬去。
senses.why: Handle also means to take in the hand, so a hand that is off its mark drops or bruises what it carries.
senses.whyCN: handle 本也有「用手拿」之意，手一失准便会把手里之物摔坏或捏坏。

senses.title: To react to someone badly
senses.definition: to respond to a person or situation in a way that makes matters worse
senses.definitionCN: 以让事情更糟的方式回应某人或某种局面
senses.example: The manager mishandled the angry customer.
senses.exampleCN: 经理没能把那位生气的顾客应付好。
senses.why: The same bad handling is applied to people, so a relationship is dropped like a clumsy object.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「弄坏」被用到了人身上，关系也像笨手手里的东西一样被摔了。

senses.title: To be careless with information
senses.definition: to store, share, or process information or personal data carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 粗心地存储、共享或处理信息及个人数据
senses.example: The clinic mishandled thousands of patient records.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所对数千份病历处理不当。
senses.why: Modern business brings a new object of bad handling: the record, the file, the data.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业给了「弄坏」一个新对象：记录、文件、数据。

senses.title: To fumble a ball
senses.definition: in ball games, to fail to hold or control the ball well
senses.definitionCN: 在球类运动中没能把球接住或控好
senses.example: The goalkeeper mishandled a simple shot.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员把一脚简单的射门接脱了手。
senses.why: Here the hand image is literal: the ball slips from a hand that mishandles it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「手」意象完全是字面的：球从没接好的手里滑脱了。

intro.en: Mishandle joins the prefix mis-, meaning wrongly, to the verb handle, which points back to the hand.
intro.cn: mishandle 由表「错误」的前缀 mis- 加动词 handle 构成，而 handle 的本源正是「手」。

items.en: Hand and its verb-related forms go back to Old English hand, the limb.
items.cn: hand 及其动词性用法可追溯到古英语 hand，即「手」。

items.en: Handel and handlen appear meaning to touch or use with the hands.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 handel 与 handlen，意为用手触碰、使用。

items.en: Handle widens from touching to managing a matter or a person.
items.cn: 十四世纪 handle 从「触碰」扩展到「处理事情或对付人」。

items.en: The prefix mis- descends from a Germanic form meaning wrongly or badly.
items.cn: 前缀 mis- 源自日耳曼语中表「错误、不好」的形式。

items.en: Mishandle is formed on mis- plus handle, meaning to handle wrongly.
items.cn: 十六世纪 mishandle 由 mis- 加 handle 构成，义为「处理失当」。

items.en: Mishandle spreads to parcels, data, and even sports mistakes.
items.cn: 现代英语把 mishandle 用到包裹、数据乃至运动失误上。

note.en: Group one shows hand words that share the handle part; group two gathers verbs of mistreatment and bungling.
note.cn: 第一组是同带 handle 的「手」词；第二组是表示虐待与弄砸的动词。

entries.definition: To deal with or touch something with your hands.
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词，义为处理或用手拿握。

entries.definition: A person who handles things or animals.
entries.definitionCN: 负责操作某物或照管动物的人。

entries.definition: The act of dealing with something badly.
entries.definitionCN: 处理失当的行为，由 mishandle 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: To treat a person or animal cruelly or unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指残忍或不公平地对待人或动物。

entries.definition: To run a business or project badly.
entries.definitionCN: 管理不善，多用于机构或项目。

entries.definition: To do a job so badly that it fails.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式用语，指把活干得一塌糊涂。

entries.definition: To carry out a task clumsily and badly.
entries.definitionCN: 指笨手笨脚地把任务搞砸。

normalIntro.en: Mishandle is mis- plus handle: the wrong way of holding, dealing, or managing.
normalIntro.cn: mishandle 就是 mis- 加 handle：拿、处理或经营的方式错了。

normal.en: Mis- means wrongly, so mishandle is handle done wrongly.
normal.cn: mis- 表错误，mishandle 即「处理错了」。

normal.en: The heavy stress falls on the first syllable of handle, not on mis.
normal.cn: 重音落在 handle 的第一个音节上，mis 不重读。

normal.en: Its usual objects are cases, goods, and data.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是案件、货物与数据。

normal.en: Mismanage goes to business; mistreat goes to people and animals.
normal.cn: 管理不善多用 mismanage，待人待物用 mistreat。

normal.en: In sports a goalkeeper may mishandle the ball.
normal.cn: 体育里守门员可能接球脱手。

abstract.en: Picture two hands shaking while carrying a tray of glasses.
abstract.cn: 想象双手端着满满一盘杯子时发抖。

abstract.en: Imagine a case file dropped into a puddle by accident.
abstract.cn: 想象案卷被不小心掉进水坑。

abstract.en: See a ball slipping through fingers at the vital moment.
abstract.cn: 看见关键时刻球从指缝里滑走。

examples.en: The museum mishandled the fragile manuscript.
examples.cn: 博物馆把那份脆弱的古抄本弄坏了。

examples.en: Mishandled luggage is a common complaint at airports.
examples.cn: 行李被粗暴装卸是机场常见投诉。

examples.en: She never mishandles a difficult question in public.
examples.cn: 她在公开场合从未把难题应付失当。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯罕逗」——密斯把名贵的「罕」见古物「逗」着玩，结果弄坏了，所以 mishandle 是处理失当、粗暴对待；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: mis-（错误）＋ handle（原义「用手拿、使手」，源自古英语 hand「手」）→ 中古英语 handlen「用手碰触、使用」→ 十四世纪 handle 扩展为「处理」→ mishandle（十六世纪）义为「以错误的方式处理或对待」。

sensesIntro.en: Mishandle starts from a hand that is off its mark, then covers bad dealing with tasks, objects, people, information, and sports.
sensesIntro.cn: mishandle 从「手没抓稳」出发，再扩展到把事情、物品、人、数据以及球类都弄得不好。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that grips carelessly, so the thing in it slips and breaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手胡乱一抓，手里的东西滑落摔坏。

branches.en: Bad dealing with a task is the main sense.
branches.cn: 把事情办糟是主要义项。

branches.en: Rough holding of an object is the literal hand sense.
branches.cn: 对物品粗暴是字面的「手」义项。

branches.en: Dealing with a person badly grows from the same image.
branches.cn: 把人应付失当由同一意象生长而来。

branches.en: Records and data are new objects of bad handling.
branches.cn: 记录与数据是「弄坏」的新对象。

branches.en: Both are literal: things or balls slip out of clumsy hands.
branches.cn: 两者皆字面：东西或球从笨手里滑脱。

intro.en: Mishandle joins a native Germanic prefix mis to the native hand word handle.
intro.cn: mishandle 是日耳曼语前缀 mis- 加上「手」的词汇 handle 组成。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin core; its parts are the Germanic prefix mis and Old English hand, with no Latin members.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语核心，构件是日耳曼语前缀 mis 与古英语 hand，并无拉丁同族词。

items.example: Mis- reverses the good sense.
items.exampleCN: mis- 把好的意思反转。

items.example: Handle alone means dealing properly.
items.exampleCN: handle 本身指处理得当。

items.example: Hand gives the handling image.
items.exampleCN: hand 提供「用手处理」的意象。

items.example: German builds the same hand word.
items.exampleCN: 德语用同样的「手」词构词。

items.example: The ending -s marks the third person.
items.exampleCN: -s 标记第三人称单数。

items.example: The ending -ed marks past forms.
items.exampleCN: -ed 标记过去形式。

items.example: The ending -ing makes a noun.
items.exampleCN: -ing 使其成为名词。

items.example: The suffix forms handler.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 handler。

items.example: A handler deals with goods or animals.
items.exampleCN: handler 负责货物或动物。

items.example: Mis- plus treat works the same way.
items.exampleCN: mis- 加 treat 的构词方式相同。

definition_zh: 小意外；（多指轻微的）不幸事故；倒霉事
definition_en: a small accident or unlucky event that causes little harm and is usually not serious
core_image: 咖啡杯在桌边一晃，倒在笔记本旁，纸上只洇开一小块
scene: 他拎着行李箱冲向月台，鞋跟却卡进井盖里。A slight mishap with the heel of his shoe cost him a minute on the way to the train.
sceneCN: 这里 mishap 是「小意外；轻微的不幸」（第 1 个义项：无伤大雅的意外小事）；句意：他的鞋跟出了点小意外，让他赶火车时耽搁了一分钟。

pos.zh: 小意外；轻微的不幸事故；倒霉事

derivatives.zh: 误闯不幸：由 mis- 加 adventure 构成，义为「意外事故；不测」
由 mis- 加 fortune 构成，义为「不幸；灾祸」，程度比 mishap 重
由 hap 加表缺少的后缀 -less 构成，义为「倒霉的；不幸的」
可能是 hap 的另一路派生（一般认为），义为「危险；风险」

senses.title: A small unlucky accident
senses.definition: an accident that is unlucky but causes little damage and is quickly overcome
senses.definitionCN: 碰巧不走运、却损害很小且很快就能过去的事故
senses.example: Apart from a few mishaps, the trip went well.
senses.exampleCN: 除了几次小意外，这趟旅行还算顺利。
senses.why: The second part of the word picks up the sense of chance, so a mishap is luck that happened to fall wrong.
senses.whyCN: 词的后半截带着「偶然、运气」之意，所以 mishap 是碰巧落空的运气。

senses.title: A trouble on a journey or plan
senses.definition: an unexpected problem that interrupts travel, work, or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 打断行程、工作或计划的意外麻烦
senses.example: He arrived without mishap late at night.
senses.exampleCN: 他深夜抵达，一路上平安无事。
senses.why: Travel is where small accidents are most often met, so the word settles into reports of journeys that had small troubles.
senses.whyCN: 旅途最容易遇上小变故，于是这个词常出现在「路上出了点岔子」的行程报告里。

senses.title: A slight physical accident
senses.titleCN: 轻微的磕碰；（报道中）小伤
senses.definition: a slight injury or mechanical slip, as in a fall or a faulty machine
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的受伤或机械上的小毛病，如摔一跤或机器出故障
senses.example: The diver was unhurt after a minor mishap.
senses.exampleCN: 跳水员在出了点小状况后并无大碍。
senses.why: News writing uses it for bodies and machines that briefly go wrong without lasting harm.
senses.whyCN: 新闻报道用它描述身体或机器短暂出毛病、却没有留下后患的情形。

intro.en: Mishap is a native English noun formed from the prefix mis- and the old noun hap, meaning chance or luck.
intro.cn: mishap 是英语本土名词，由前缀 mis- 与古名词 hap（运气、机会）合成。

items.en: Happ comes from Old Norse, meaning luck or chance.
items.cn: hap 源自古代北欧语，意为运气或机会。

items.en: Hap is used for fortune, whether good or bad.
items.cn: 中古英语中 hap 泛指好运或坏运。

items.en: Mis- joins hap to name ill luck.
items.cn: 十四世纪 mis- 与 hap 结合，表示「厄运」。

items.en: The sense narrows to a small unlucky accident.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义收缩为「小意外」。

items.en: Newspapers use mishap for minor accidents in travel and sport.
items.cn: 现代报纸用它报道旅行与体育中的小事故。

note.en: Group one shows the hap family of luck words; group two holds words for accidents and bad luck.
note.cn: 第一组是同带 hap「运气」的词；第二组是表示事故与倒霉的词语。

entries.definition: Chance or luck, often in the older sense of fortune.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧用法，指机会或运气，多带旧式色彩。

entries.definition: To take place by chance.
Chosen by chance rather than plan.
entries.definitionCN: 随意而不是按计划地，保留「碰巧」之义。

entries.definition: Possibly, literally by chance.
An event that happens unexpectedly.
entries.definitionCN: 近义，指意外发生的事件，范围更广。

entries.definition: Serious bad luck with lasting consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 更重的不幸，后果更持久。

entries.definition: An unlucky accident in formal or legal use.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或法律用语中的不幸事故。

normalIntro.en: Mishap pairs mis- with hap, the old word for chance, so it means luck that came out wrong.
normalIntro.cn: mishap 把 mis- 与旧词 hap（机会、运气）配对，意思是「碰巧走偏的运气」。

normal.en: Stress sits on the first syllable: MIS-hap.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：MIS-hap。

normal.en: A mishap is small and is usually quickly forgotten.
normal.cn: mishap 通常很小，很快就被忘掉。

normal.en: The phrase without mishap means safely and smoothly.
normal.cn: without mishap 意为平安无事。

normal.en: Its relatives happen and perhaps keep the old chance sense.
normal.cn: 同族的 happen 与 perhaps 都保留「碰巧」之义。

normal.en: For lasting harm use disaster, not mishap.
normal.cn: 若要强调严重后果，用 disaster 而不用 mishap。

abstract.en: See a paper cup tipping just enough to spill a little tea.
abstract.cn: 看见纸杯刚好一歪，洒出一点茶。

abstract.en: Imagine a car tyre that hisses but still rolls on.
abstract.cn: 想象一只车胎漏气嘶嘶响却还能继续滚。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with one small smudge near a busy day.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上一个忙碌日子旁边有一小块污渍。

examples.en: The wedding went ahead without mishap.
examples.cn: 婚礼顺利举行，没有出任何岔子。

examples.en: A mishap with the printer delayed the report.
examples.cn: 打印机出了点小毛病，报告被耽搁了。

examples.en: Despite several mishaps, the expedition reached camp.
examples.cn: 尽管出了几次小意外，考察队还是回到了营地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯暗捕」——密斯在暗中捕鸟，结果扑了个空，还摔了一跤，这就是 mishap「小意外」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: mis-（错误、不好）＋ hap（运气、机会，源自古诺斯语）→ 中古英语 mis- 加 hap 表「厄运」→ 现代英语 mishap 指「小意外、轻微不幸」，核心义「碰巧落空的运气」。

sensesIntro.en: Mishap goes from luck that fell wrong to a small accident, then to the troubles of a journey and to slight injuries in news reports.
sensesIntro.cn: mishap 从「落空的运气」到小意外，再到旅途中的波折与新闻报道里的轻微磕碰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup tipping just enough to leave one small stain.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子刚好一歪，只洇出一小块污迹。

branches.en: A small unlucky accident is the central sense.
branches.cn: 小小的不走运事故是中心义项。

branches.en: Trip and plan troubles extend the accident to whole journeys.
branches.cn: 行程与计划的波折把事故扩展到整段旅程。

branches.en: Slight injuries and slips form the physical sense.
branches.cn: 轻微受伤与磕碰构成身体层面的义项。

branches.en: Both are small, though one is sharp and one stretched out.
branches.cn: 两者都是小事，一个点状，一个拉长在旅途中。

branches.en: Both usually appear with without, meaning safe arrival.
branches.cn: 两者常与 without 连用，表示平安无事。

intro.en: Mishap is a Germanic compound: the prefix mis- plus the ancient noun hap for luck, with no Latin prefix involved.
intro.cn: mishap 是日耳曼语复合词：前缀 mis- 加上古老的运气名词 hap，不涉及拉丁前缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is purely Germanic and Old Norse in origin, so it has no Latin family members.
latinIntro.cn: 此词纯属日耳曼语与古代北欧语来源，没有拉丁语同族词。

items.example: Mis- turns hap into bad luck.
items.exampleCN: mis- 把 hap 变成厄运。

items.example: Hap is the old luck word.
items.exampleCN: hap 是古老的运气词。

items.example: Happen shares the same root.
items.exampleCN: happen 同出此根。

items.example: Perhaps keeps by chance.
items.exampleCN: perhaps 保留「凭运气」之意。

items.example: Hap and hazard combine here.
items.exampleCN: hap 与 hazard 在此复合。

items.example: Mis- joins adventure the same way.
items.exampleCN: mis- 以同样方式接 adventure。

items.example: Mis- plus fortune is heavier.
items.exampleCN: mis- 加 fortune 语气更重。

items.example: The ending forms mishaps.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成复数 mishaps。

definition_zh: 判断错误；误判；看错（人或情况）；（对距离、时间的）估计失误
definition_en: to form a wrong opinion or estimate about a person, situation, amount, or timing
core_image: 法官把秤看偏了一眼，砝码还停在托盘上就敲下了判决
scene: 他看到那道大水沟，以为一跳能过去，结果落在了边上。He misjudged the width of the ditch and landed in the mud.
sceneCN: 这里 misjudge 是「判断错误；估计失误」（第 1 个义项：就人或情况做出错误判断）；句意：他误判了水沟的宽度，结果掉进泥里。

pos.zh: 判断错误；误判；看错；（对距离、时间的）估计失误

derivatives.zh: 由 misjudge 加 -ment 名词化，义为「错误判断；误判」（英式拼写）
同上名词的美式拼写，义为「误判」
judge 加 -ment 构成，义为「判断；判断力」
由前缀 pre-（之前）加 judge 构成，义为「预先判断；预断」

senses.title: To form a wrong opinion
senses.definition: to form an opinion about a person or situation that later proves to be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者情况形成后来被证明是错的看法
senses.example: I misjudged him completely.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全看错了他。
senses.why: The prefix mis- flips judge, so the weighing of evidence ends with the wrong verdict.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 mis- 把 judge（判断）翻了过来，衡量证据之后却给出了错的结论。

senses.title: To estimate wrongly
senses.definition: to estimate a distance, amount, or time incorrectly
senses.definitionCN: 错误地估计距离、数量或时间
senses.example: She misjudged the length of the jump.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有拿准那一跳能有多远。
senses.why: Judging also covers measuring by eye, so a wrong measure of space or time is a misjudgement too.
senses.whyCN: 判断也包括凭眼睛目测，量错空间或时间同样算误判。

senses.title: To act on a wrong reading
senses.titleCN: 因误判而失手；把人拿捏错了
senses.definition: to deal with a person or a chance badly because you read them wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 因为看错了人或时机，把事情处理得不好
senses.example: The driver misjudged the turn and scraped the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 司机误判了那个弯，刮坏了墙。
senses.why: From a wrong reading to a wrong move: the error passes from the mind into the action.
senses.whyCN: 从看错到做错：错误从头脑里转移到了行动上。

intro.en: Misjudge pairs the prefix mis- with the verb judge, which goes back through Latin to laws and decisions.
intro.cn: misjudge 由前缀 mis- 加动词 judge 组成，而 judge 经过去拉丁语可以追到法律与裁决。

items.en: Judex means one who passes judgment, built on ius law and dicere to say.
items.cn: 拉丁语 judex 指作出判决的人，由 ius（法）与 dicere（说）构成。

items.en: Judicare means to judge, to decide a case in law.
items.cn: judicare 意为评判、依法裁决。

items.en: Jugier carries the verb into French in the twelfth century.
items.cn: 十二世纪 jugier 把该动词带入法语。

items.en: Juggen appears in English for deciding and for forming opinions.
items.cn: 中古英语 juggen 既指裁决，也指形成看法。

items.en: Mis- plus judge yields misjudge, to judge wrongly.
items.cn: 十七世纪 mis- 与 judge 合成 misjudge，义为误判。

items.en: Modern use covers distances, moments, and behaviour as well as people.
items.cn: 现代用法既评人，也用于距离、时机与举止。

note.en: Group one holds the judge family; group two holds verbs of wrong belief and wrong estimate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 judge 的词族；第二组是表示误认与误估的动词。

entries.definition: To form an opinion or decide a case.
entries.definitionCN: 基础词，义为评判或审理。

entries.definition: An opinion or the ability to decide well.
entries.definitionCN: 由 judge 加 -ment 构成，指判断或判断力。

entries.definition: To decide before hearing the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 未了解事实便预先下判断。

entries.definition: Of courts and the work of judging.
entries.definitionCN: 同源，指与法院及审判有关的。

entries.definition: To understand the meaning of something wrongly.
To calculate or expect amounts wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 算错或预料错了数量，多用于数字。

entries.definition: To judge something to be smaller than it is.

normalIntro.en: Misjudge is mis- plus judge: a verdict reached without the evidence.
normalIntro.cn: misjudge 是 mis- 加 judge：没等证据齐全就下了结论。

normal.en: Stress sits on the second syllable: mis-JUDGE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节：mis-JUDGE。

normal.en: Its objects are often people, situations, distances, and moments.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是人、形势、距离与时机。

normal.en: The past form misjudged is common after badly and grossly.
normal.cn: 过去式 misjudged 常跟 badly 与 grossly 连用。

normal.en: Judge is the base; mis- only adds the sense of wrong.
normal.cn: judge 是基础词，mis- 只加上「错误」的意思。

normal.en: Compare mistake for a thing done; misjudge is about a belief or an estimate.
normal.cn: 对比 mistake：mistake 指做错的事，misjudge 指看错、估错。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden scale with weights still hanging off the hook.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆木秤，砝码还挂在钩子外面没放上盘。

abstract.en: See a tape measure laid across a stream that is wider than it looked.
abstract.cn: 看见卷尺丈量的小河比看上去要宽得多。

abstract.en: Imagine a car taking a corner too tight and kissing the kerb.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车转弯切得太里，蹭上了路缘。

examples.en: Do not misjudge the pace of the current.
examples.cn: 别低估了水流的速度。

examples.en: The jury misjudged the honesty of the witness.
examples.cn: 陪审团判断错了证人的诚信。

examples.en: Nobody misjudges her ability to stay calm.
examples.cn: 没有人会错看她保持冷静的能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯扎吉」——密斯扎了一记歪针，把病人看得错上加错，所以 misjudge 是误判、看错；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: mis-（错误）＋ judge（判断；源自拉丁语 judicare、judex，由 ius「法」与 dicere「说」构成）→ misjudge（十七世纪），核心义「把秤看错、把话说成错判」。

sensesIntro.en: Misjudge runs from a wrong opinion about people, to a wrong estimate of space and time, to a wrong move made on the strength of that error.
sensesIntro.cn: misjudge 从对人的错误看法，到对距离与时间的误估，再到由这个错误引出的错误举动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a judge who reads the scale before the weights settle.
core.cn: 核心意象：法官在砝码还没稳住时就宣读了判决。

branches.en: A wrong opinion about people is the main branch.
branches.cn: 对人的错误看法是主要分支。

branches.en: Wrong estimates of space and time extend the verdict to measurement.
branches.cn: 对空间与时间的误估把判决延伸到测量。

branches.en: Wrong readings lead straight to wrong actions.
branches.cn: 看错直接导致做错。

branches.en: One person is misread, then handled badly on that reading.
branches.cn: 先看错一个人，再据此把人处理错了。

branches.en: A distance is misjudged, then the turn is taken wrong.
branches.cn: 先误判距离，再把那个弯转错了。

intro.en: Misjudge joins a Germanic prefix to a verb that reached English through Latin, French, and law courts.
intro.cn: misjudge 把日耳曼语前缀接在一个经拉丁语、法语与法庭传入英语的动词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius and dicere build judex and judicare; judicare becomes French jugier and English judge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius 与 dicere 构成 judex 与 judicare，judicare 再经法语 jugier 变成英语 judge。

items.example: Mis- flips judge to misjudge.
items.exampleCN: mis- 把 judge 变成 misjudge。

items.example: Judge is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: judge 是基础动词。

items.example: Judex joins law and saying.
items.exampleCN: judex 由「法」与「说」合成。

items.example: Judicare is the direct Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: judicare 是直接的拉丁动词。

items.example: Jus hides inside judex.
items.exampleCN: jus 藏在 judex 之中。

items.example: Dicere gives the speaking half.
items.exampleCN: dicere 提供「说」这一半。

items.example: The suffix forms misjudgement.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀构成 misjudgement。

items.example: Misjudging is the act in progress.
items.exampleCN: misjudging 指正在进行中的那个误判动作。

items.example: The prefix pre- means before.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 表示「之前」。
